blocks.text: Reformist Movements started in India due to:
1. Social evilsin society that existed in forms of untouchability, superstition, polygamy (multiple marriages), purdah system, polytheism (worship of more than one God), ete.
2. Position of women deteriorated in society due to polygamy, Sati system and also because widow remarriage was not allowed.
Steps taken to Ameliorate Women's Position 1. Abolition of Sati
1829: An Act passed to abolish Sati System with the efforts of Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Lord William Bentinck was the then Governor-General of India).
2. Widow Remarriage
1856: Widow Remarriage Act passed with efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar [Got this title from his college (Principal in Sanskrit College)]
+ The Act was drafted during the tenure of Lord Dalhousie and enacted in 1856 under Lord Canning.
+ Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was against child marriage.
Widow Remarriage Association by:
+ 1853: Vishnu Shastri Pandit formed Vidhava Vivaha Uttejaka Mandal.
1861:M. G. Ranadeformeda Widow Remarriage Association.
+ Satyaprakash was a Gujarati language weekly founded by social reformer and journalist Karsondas Mulji with an intention of social reform.
3. Child Marriage
+ 1891: Age of Consent Act passed due to the efforts of B.
M. Malabari (child marriage less than 12 years was not allowed)
Sarda Act of 1929: It is also known as Child Marriage Restraint Act through which minimum age for marriage at 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys was set.
4. Education + 1835: Thomas Babington Macaulay presented Macaulay's Minute to promote English education in India.
He gave Downward Filtration Theory.
Lord William Bentinck (Father of English Education in India) was the Governor-General of India during this time.
1854: Wood's Dispatch
It rejected the Downward Filtration Theory.
It is also known as Magna Carta of Indian Education.
According to Wood's Dispatch Primary level education should be given in Vernacular; Secondary level education in Anglo-Vernacular; Higher level education in English.
5. Certain Women's Organisation Formed
Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910) > Founder: Sarla Devi Chaudhurani.
Ladies Social Conference (1904) + Founder: Ramabai Ranade.
Women's Indian Association (1917) + Annie Besant, Margaret Cousins and Jeena Raja Dasa.
National Council of Women in India (1925) + Lady Meherbai Tata.
All India Women's Conference (1927) — Founder:
Arya Mahila Samaj (1882) > Founder: Pandita Ramabai Saraswati.
Ist university for Indian Women (SNDT): by Dr Dhondo Keshav Karve (1916).
Struggle against Caste based Exploitation (against Chaturvarna System)
Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924): It was established by B. R. Ambedkar at Bombay.
+ Self Respect Movement (1925) It was started by E. V.
Ramaswamy Naicker in Tamil Nadu.
Same movement started by:
Narayan Guru in Kerala.
Jyotiba Phule in Maharashtra.
+ Mahad Satyagraha (1927): It was led by B. R. Ambedkar {he also burnt Manusmriti (ancient text upholding caste laws)} Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Brahmo Samaj
Heis known as "Father of Indian Renaissance".
+ He was given the title of "Raja" by Akbar II.
1814:Heestablished Atmiya Sabhain Calcutta (Forerunner of Brahmo Samaj).
1817: He founded Hindu College in Calcutta with the help of David Hare.
1825: He established Vedanta College.
+ 1828:RajaRam Mohan Roy founded Brahmo Sabha,which later became the Brahmo Samaj.
He also translated Vedas in Bengali.
He was against idol worship, polytheism, child marriage.

+ 1839: He started Tattvabodhini Sabha along with its organ Tattvabodhini Patrika in Bengali in Calcutta.
1858: He invited Keshab Chandra Sen to join the Brahmo Samaj.
Due to difference in philosophical thinking, Brahmo Samaj split into two in 1866, namely Brahmo Samaj of India (led by Keshab Chandra Sen) and Adi Brahmo Samaj (led by Debendranath Tagore).
Later Adi Brahmo Samaj also got divided and Sadharan Brahmo Samaj was founded by Ananda Mohan Bose in Veda Samaj
1864: Veda Samaj was formed in Madras by Keshab Chandra Sen and K. Sridharalu Naidu.
It is also known as Brahmo Samaj of South India.
Young Bengal Movement (Late 1820s and Early 1830s)
Started by: Henry Vivian Derozia.
He was a teacher at the Hindu College.
Dharma Sabha > Revivalist Movement (1830)
It was started by Radhakanta Deb — He was against the idea of Brahmo Samaj.
Paramhansa Mandali (1849) — (**SSC considers this year as 1840)
It was formed by Dadoba Pandurang and Durgaram Mehtaji in Maharashtra.
Prarthana Samaj (1867)
It was formed by Atmaram Pandurang in Maharashtra.
M.G. Ranade joined it in 1870, R G Bhandarkar was also a member.
Deoband Movement (1866)
Started by: Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi.
Launched in: Saharanpur district in Uttar Pradesh.
Singh Sabha Movement (1873)
It started in Amritsar.
Itaimed to revive Sikh faith by bringing back the converts.
Satyasodhak Samaj (1873)
It was formed by Jyotiba Phule (he was from Mali/ Gardener community) in Maharashtra against caste discrimination.
In 1848, Jyotiba Phule along with his wife Savitri Phule (first female teacher of India) started the first school for girls in Pune.
Books written by Jyotiba Phule: Gulamgiri, Sarvajanik Satyadharma (both in Marathi).
Arya Samaj (1875)
It was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati (original name: Mool Shankar).
+ First unit of Arya Samaj was opened at Bombay and later · shifted to Lahore.
He advocated for Caste less and Class less society.
He gave slogans "Go Back to Vedas" and "India for Indians".
He considered Vedas as infallible but criticised Puranas.
He believed in Karma and Reincarnation.
He subscribed (support) the Chaturvarna system on the basis of work not by birth.
He was against the Idol Worship.
Book written by him: Satyarth Prakash.
1886: Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) College in Lahore was established in memory of Swami Dayanand by Mahatma Hansraj.
1893: The Arya Samaj members in Punjab were divided on the question of vegetarianism and modem education.
The group that refrained from eating meat were called the "Mahatma" group and the other group, the "Cultured Party".
Aligarh Movement (1875)
Started by: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
He established a Mohammaden Anglo Oriental College in 1875 which was later called Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
He also founded Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.
Magazine: Tahdhib-ul-Akhlaq (improvement of manners and morals).
Dev Samaj (1887)
Founder: Shiv Narayan Agnihotri at Lahore.
It wasa purification movement initiated by the Arya Samaj to reconvert people who had converted to other religions (especially Islam and Christianity) back to Hinduism.
Hestarted the Ramkrishna Movement.
Original Name: Narendranath Dutta.
His birth: 12 Jan 1863 is celebrated as "National Youth Day".
Died on: 4 July 1902.
He believed in idol worship.
Books written: Raja Yoga, Karma Yoga.
1893: Swami Vivekananda gave a speech in Chicago (USA) in a conference.
He advocated on how to make balance between Materialism and Spiritualism.
Swami Vivekananda Rock Memorial is in Tamil Nadu (Kanyakumari).
Ramkrishna Mission/Ramkrishna Movement (1897)
+ It was started by Swami Vivekananda in the memory of his Guru Ramkrishna Paramhansa (Priest of Kali Mandir in Calcutta) > Original name: Gadadhar Chattopadhyay.
HQ: Belur Math; Howrah (West Bengal).
+ According to him "Service to man is service to God".
+ He started two newspapers: Darpan and Digdarshan.
He is remembered as the "Father of Marathi Journalism".
He started weekly newspapers: Prabhakar and Hitechhu.
He started a weekly: Sudharak.
Servants of India Society (1905)
Founder: Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
He was political Guru of Gandhi and Jinnah.
To promote education and social service in India.
Seva Sadan (1908)
Founder: B. M. Malabari.
+ He worked against child marriage and for widow remarriage.
Social Service League (1911)
Founder: Narayana Malhar Joshi at Bombay.
He also started All India Trade Union Congress in 1920.
Faraizi Movement (1818)
Wahabi Movement
Started by: Haji Shariatullah
Started by: Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi of Rae Bareli.
It was a Muslim revivalist movement, popularly known as Tariqa-e-Muhammadiya.
Syed Ahmad Barelvi and his followers worked to transform India from Dar-ul-Harb (land of non-Islamic rule) into Dar-ul-Islam (land governed by Islamic principles).
It started in 1820s in Chhatisgarh region by Guru Ghasidas who belonged to Satnami sect.
He worked with the leatherworkers (around 1820) to improve their social status.
Theosophical Society (1875)
+ It was started in New York (USA) by HP Blavatsky and HS Olcott.:
The society's HQ was shifted to Adyar Madras from New York in 1882.
+ Later Annie Besant took its membership.
+ This society was highly influenced by Hindu belief system.
Indian National Social Conference (1887)
Founders: M. G. Ranade and Raghunath Rao.
Pledge Movement was started by them against child marriage.
Shree Narayana Guru Dharam Paripalana (SNDP)
+ Started by: Shree Narayan Guru Swami for the upliftment of Ezhavas Community of Kerala.
Important slogan: "Oru Jathi, Oru Matham, Oru Daivam"
(One Caste, One Religion, One God for All).
Justice Movement (1917)
Started by: C. N. Mudaliar, T. M. Nair and P. Tyagaraja.
Self Respect Movement (1925)
Founder: E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker (also known as Periyar) in Tamil Nadu.
Objective: Rejection of Brahminical dominance and rituals.
Note: The Civil Disobedience Movement in Kerala was led by K. Kelappan.
Amar Jiban by Rassundari Devi > 1st known autobiography written by an Indian Woman.
Temple Entry Movement (for the entry of Dalits in temple)
Temple entry movement was started by Dr B.R. Ambedkar in 1927.
In South India (1924), it was started by T. K. Madhavan.
Vaikom Satyagraha (1924), it was started by K.P. Kesava Menon.
Stri Purush Tulna was written by: Tarabai Shinde.
B. R. Ambedkar started Temple Entry Movement in 1930 here for the entry of Dalits in this temple
